name: English
reset_buttons_note: Note: only clears actions set in this app. Key remaps set in Windows BaseCamp (e.g. Shift+Tab, Suspend) are stored in the keyboard's firmware and can only be removed in Windows BaseCamp.
no_device_hint: Connect your Mountain device, or pick another tab above.
no_access_title: The device is here, but cannot be opened
no_access_hint: No permission for {nodes}. The udev rule that grants access is missing or has not been applied. Install 99-mountain.rules into /etc/udev/rules.d/, then run: sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger, and replug the device.
settings_restore_confirm: This will overwrite your current settings. Continue?
settings_picker_reset_hint: Forget the last folder used for each file picker. Next time the picker opens at $ICON_PATH (if set) or /usr/share/icons.
settings_picker_reset_ok: Forgotten. pickers will reset on next open.
settings_update_hint_appimage: Download the new AppImage from github.com/ramisotti13-eng/BaseCamp-Linux/releases and replace the current file.
settings_update_hint_arch: Run: yay -Syu basecamp-linux  (or your AUR helper)
settings_update_hint_debian: Run: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade basecamp-linux  (or download the .deb from Releases)
settings_update_hint_source: Pull the latest changes: git pull
settings_update_done: Update installed. restart BaseCamp Linux to finish.
settings_update_no_asset: No matching AppImage in the release.
update_dialog_body: BaseCamp Linux v{ver} is available. Update now?
settings_profile_loaded: Profile "{name}" loaded ({n} files). restart to apply
settings_profile_load_confirm: Load profile "{name}"? Current settings will be overwritten.
side_leds_hint: Lights the 44-LED perimeter ring in one colour. Uses custom RGB mode and keeps your last per-key colours on the main keys; a running effect above is replaced (re-apply it to switch back).
multi_upload_empty: No images yet, upload one first
dp_hue_unpaired: (pair the Hue bridge first, under Philips Hue)
dp_quirk_hint: DisplayPad detected but its USB command interface is missing, see README (usbhid quirk fix)
dp_dialog_hint: Left-click: pick image  ·  Right-click: clear slot
dp_pick_fullscreen: Pick fullscreen (image or GIF, all 12 buttons)
dp_gif_not_animated: No animated GIF found, load as static image?
dp_startup_help: The picture the DisplayPad shows when it is plugged in (800 x 240). It is stored in the DisplayPad.
dp_startup_unknown: The current one cannot be read from the pad
dp_startup_confirm: The start-up picture is stored permanently in the DisplayPad. The Mountain logo cannot be restored afterwards.
dp_startup_writing: Writing the start-up picture… (about 10 seconds, do not unplug)
dp_startup_done: Start-up picture saved. It shows the next time the DisplayPad is plugged in.
action_type_text_hint: Text to type when key is pressed
macro_no_macros: No macros, click '+ New Macro' to create one
macro_rec_space_hint: Space = Start/Stop  |  Move the mouse freely
macro_no_tool: xdotool or ydotool not found. Install: sudo dnf/apt/pacman install xdotool
macro_rec_empty: No mouse movement captured. Is xdotool or python-xlib installed?
macro_rec_no_recordings: No recordings yet, use 'Rec Mouse' first
pluginmgr_empty:
No plugins installed -- drop a plugin folder into
~/.config/mountain-time-sync/plugins/ and restart
pluginmgr_restart: Restart the app for full effect (panel changes)
pluginmgr_install_hint: Paste a GitHub URL or browse to a plugin folder
pluginmgr_newer_installed: v{have} is installed, a higher version than the published v{pub}, so no update is offered for it. If you did not raise the version yourself, install the published one.
plugin_updates_one: An update is available for 1 plugin
pluginmgr_other_copy: the copy in {path} is the one that runs
pluginmgr_is_link: {path} is a link to {target} and was left as it is
dp_delete_page_main_error: The Main page can't be deleted, it's just the page the app opens on.
dp_delete_page_referenced_warning: "{name}" is still targeted by {count} button(s)/timeout(s). Deleting it will leave those pointing at a page that no longer exists:
nav_no_devices: No device found. Check the USB permissions, see the README.
settings_update_current: You are on {ver}, the latest version.
settings_backup_hint: Key assignments, DisplayPad pages, macros, OBS and profiles in one ZIP. Image libraries and plugins stay out so the file stays small.
dp_grid_hint: Click a key to edit it, right-click clears it
dp_note_text: Shown in a small box when you switch to this page, from a key on the pad, the tray or a script, together with the hints of its keys. A page with neither stays silent. The key hints are written beside the grid, one key at a time.
dp_note_show: Show the box when switching to this page
dp_note_timeout: Close the box after (seconds, 0 keeps it open)
macro_unassigned: Not assigned to any key yet
pluginmgr_requires_missing: Needs {pkg}, not available here. The AppImage ships its own Python and cannot see packages installed with the system pip, so this plugin only works on a source install.
pluginmgr_pick_hint: Pick a plugin on the left
mp_type_missing: Bound to “{type}”, which is not installed here
mp_custom_hint: Custom lights each key in the colour you gave it. Pick a key on the left, choose its colour, then apply.
mp_hint_shell: Command to run, e.g. flatpak run com.spotify.Client
mp_hint_url: Address to open in the browser
mp_hint_folder: Folder to open in the file manager
mp_hint_macro: Name of a macro from the Macros screen
toolkit_notice_title: CustomTkinter is newer than this version
toolkit_notice_body: CustomTkinter {ver} is installed, and this version of BaseCamp Linux does not support it fully yet. The dropdowns use CustomTkinter's own menus for now. Update BaseCamp Linux, or install the CustomTkinter version it supports.
toolkit_notice_detail:
Update:  git pull
Or:  pip install "customtkinter<{below}"
web_fallback_title: The new interface could not start
web_fallback_body_appimage: This AppImage is older than BaseCamp Linux 4.0 and has no web view, and the update that brought 4.0 carries program files only. So the classic interface started. Download the new AppImage from the release page to get the new interface; your settings stay as they are.
web_fallback_body_install: pywebview or a web view for it is missing here, so the classic interface started. Install them as the README describes (Installation, From source) and start BaseCamp Linux again.
web_fallback_detail:
Reason: {why}
The classic interface starts directly with --classic.
dp_insp_hint_ph: A few words, shown when the page comes up
shell_settings_later: More settings arrive in a later step.
shell_device_later: This device's screen is not part of the new interface yet.
dp_discard_msg: The key has changes that were not applied. Discard them?
dp_key_select: Select a key to edit its binding.
dp_debounce_help: Ignore repeated presses within this time.
dp_min_ms_help: Shortest time per animation frame, in milliseconds.
mk_busy: The mouse is still busy with the last lighting change.
mk_debounce_help: Time a button press is held back to filter out double clicks.
mk_left_warn: Taking away the left click has to be confirmed within a few seconds, otherwise it is put back.
mk_preset_help: Loading a preset only fills the editor; Apply sends it to the mouse.
mk_preset_loaded: Preset loaded. Apply to send it to the mouse.
mk_remap_reverting: Time is up, putting the old function back…
mk_reset_msg: Put every button back to its default function? This is saved here; the mouse keeps what it has until a button is assigned again.
mk_select_hint: Select a button on the mouse or in the list.
mk_set_poll_help: How often the mouse reports its position to the computer. Higher is smoother and uses more of the processor.
mk_set_dpi_help: Drag a marker or type a value. A click on a level makes it the active one.
mk_reset_all_msg: Resets the five DPI levels (active: level 1), polling rate, button response time, lift-off distance and angle snapping to the application's defaults. Not reset: the lighting and the button assignments (they have their own pages).
mk_sniper_help: Sniper DPI applies while the button is held, at least {min}.
em_dock_help: Custom mode must be active on the dial for the media dock buttons to work with alternative functions.
em_flash_note: A picture is written into the keyboard's flash: this takes 45 to 60 seconds. You can keep using the app meanwhile; do not unplug the keyboard.
em_upload_msg: The picture is written into the keyboard's flash. This takes 45 to 60 seconds, Monitor Mode pauses meanwhile, and the keyboard must stay connected until it is done.
em_job_main_upload: Writing the picture to the display…
em_job_reset_buttons: Clearing the D-key actions in the flash…
em_job_dpush: Writing a plugin picture to a D-key…
em_main_same: The display shows this picture already
em_dd_loading: Reading the settings from the keyboard…
em_dd_no_answer: The keyboard did not answer, so these settings can't be changed right now: {err}
em_pk_fx_tip: Click keys to set individual RGB effects, or drag a selection frame to change the effects of several keys at once.
em_ind_reset_msg: Every key and the ring LEDs become static white, on the keyboard too. This cannot be undone.
em_job_per_key_fx: Sending the key effects and saving them in the keyboard…
em_fw_busy: A picture is being written to the keyboard; read the versions again in a minute.
em_mon_paused: Paused for a moment: the keyboard is busy with another job
em_mon_ended: Monitor Mode ended by itself (exit code {code})
em_mon_help: Monitor Mode sends the numbers to the display and runs the D-key actions. A job such as an upload pauses it and brings it back.
em_sync_help: Sends the computer's time to the dial.
em_reset_msg: Writes the D-key actions into the keyboard's flash again, which clears the actions this app set.
em_set_game_help: Switches off the chosen key combinations while the keyboard is in game mode, so a game is not interrupted. Game mode is switched on and off on the keyboard with Fn + Pause; an LED on the media dock shows it.
em_set_game_toggle: On and off on the keyboard: Fn + Pause
em_set_leds_help: Switches the keyboard's indicator LEDs on or off.
em_board_failed: The keyboard did not answer, its settings are not shown.
em_reset_all_msg: The keyboard is reset to factory settings: lighting, key assignments, macros in the keyboard, pictures on D1–D4 and the dial, dial settings. The active Everest Max profile is reset as well.
em_job_factory_reset: Resetting the keyboard to factory settings…
em_factory_done: The keyboard is back to factory settings
e60_no_controls: This effect has nothing to set.
e60_perkey_hint: Click selects, Ctrl+click adds, Shift+click selects a range, Alt+click picks a key's colour.
e60_nothing_saved: No lighting saved yet; the keyboard keeps its own.
e60_layout_help: ANSI or ISO is read from the keyboard. The lighting is saved and sent again when the keyboard is plugged in.
mp_save_help: Save to pad keeps the lighting on the MacroPad when it runs without BaseCamp.
set_macro_discard_msg: This macro has changes that were not saved. Discard them?
set_macro_delete_confirm: Delete macro "{name}"? Keys that use it will do nothing.
set_macro_pick: Pick a macro on the left, or create a new one.
set_macro_no_steps: No steps yet. Add one below.
set_macro_delay_own: A delay step waits by its own value
set_macro_steps_help: Steps run from top to bottom. Each key step holds one key: use Key Down and Key Up around other steps for combinations. Rec names the next key you press on this page.
set_macro_rec_key_title: Record the next key you press
set_macro_key_unknown: That key has no name in macros. Pick one from the list.
set_macro_path_note: Recorded mouse path ({file}), made in the classic interface
set_obs_help: BaseCamp connects to OBS Studio over its WebSocket server (Tools, WebSocket Server Settings in OBS).
set_obs_password_help: Leave it empty to keep the saved password.
set_plugin_err_bad_source: That is neither a folder nor a GitHub URL
set_plugin_refresh: Reload the list of published plugins
set_plugin_panel_only: This plugin has a panel that can only be shown in the classic interface. Its actions and services work here.
photo_hint_title: This is a drawing. The device photos of Mountain's Base Camp can be taken over: Settings → Device photos & icons, then run the import there.
photo_hint_show: Show the hint on the drawings again
set_photos_explain: The photos are read from your own Mountain Base Camp and copied to your configuration. BaseCamp Linux never ships them.
set_photos_none: Not imported: the drawings are shown
set_photos_err_not_found: No Mountain Base Camp installation found. Choose its folder.
set_photos_err_no_images: That folder has none of the device pictures.
set_photos_download_confirm: This downloads about 260 MB from Mountain's server. Only the device photos are kept; the download is deleted afterwards.
set_dl_err_network: Could not reach the server. Check your connection.
set_dl_err_not_found: The file was not found on the server.
set_dl_err_bad_package: The file is not a usable package.
set_packs_explain: Ready-made icons you can put on DisplayPad keys. The Mountain pack has 57 icons.
dp_lib_empty: Nothing here yet. Pictures you give a key are kept in the library, and icon packs from the Settings show up here too.
ie_nopic: Pick a picture with Browse, or from your pictures, to crop it.
ie_crop_box: Crop box (arrow keys move it, + and - resize it)
ie_gif: GIF · {n} frames: the crop applies to every frame
ie_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}" from your pictures? Keys that use it lose their picture.
ie_err_too_many_frames: The animation has too many frames.
ie_err_bad_format: This is not a picture that can be read (jpg, png, bmp, gif or webp).
ie_err_not_found: The file is not there any more.
ie_err_bad_crop: The crop box does not fit the picture.
ie_err_not_allowed: Only your own pictures can be deleted.
set_pack_basecamp: Base Camp icons (10 categories: Default, Adobe, DaVinci, OBS, Twitch, YouTube, Spotify, Zoom)
set_pack_basecamp_help: Taken from your Base Camp installation if one is found, otherwise from the Base Camp package on mountain.gg.
kbl_help: The keyboard does not tell its layout, so the pictures use the system's layout unless you choose one.
kbf_no_numpad: No numpad attached: the display keys D1-D4 sit on it.
mod_help: The keyboard does not always report its modules. Automatic uses its answer when it gives one, otherwise both are shown.
mod_source_assumed: Assumed: the keyboard has not reported its modules.
dp_auto_off_help: After this long without a key press the keys go dark. The next press only turns them back on.
dp_auto_off_zero: Enter a time of at least one second.
dp_lock_label: While the computer is locked or asleep
dp_lock_help: When the computer locks or goes to sleep, the DisplayPad shows a clock, your own picture or the BaseCamp logo across its keys, or turns off. Unlocking brings the page back; meanwhile the keys do nothing.
dp_lock_unwatched: This desktop's lock and sleep signals cannot be followed (gdbus is missing), so the pad keeps its pages.
home_no_devices: No device is plugged in. Plug one in and it shows up here.
mk_led_help: Pick one or more squares (Ctrl-click or drag for several), then set the colour.
em_dd_custom_tip: Custom mode must be active for the keys bound to the media dock to work with alternative functions
em_dd_screensaver_tip: This picture appears on the Display Dial when it is not active. Configurable, the default is the MOUNTAIN logo
em_dd_content_tip: The default is the MOUNTAIN logo; replace it with a picture of your own or another function
em_dd_reset_tip: Affects the Display Dial configuration only
em_dd_reset_confirm: Reset the Display Dial's menus, menu colour, screensaver and turn-off to Base Camp's defaults?
emk_select: Click a key in the picture to bind it.
emk_no_free_fkey: At most {max} keys can run something in the app (each through an F-key between F13 and F24), and all {max} are taken.
emk_app_note: The key sends {f}; the app runs the action when it hears {f} ({n} of {max} still free).
emk_in_keyboard: The macro is written into the keyboard and runs without the app too.
emk_listener_denied: The app may not read the keyboard's input device (/dev/input). Install the current 99-mountain.rules and plug the keyboard in again.
emk_dkey_app_note: D1 to D4 run an action while Monitor Mode is on.
emk_dock_app_note: What the dock buttons send for an action is not known yet: it is saved, but pressing does nothing yet.
emk_no_macros: No macros yet: create one under Settings → Macros.
prof_program_label: Activate this profile when this program starts:
prof_reset_confirm: Reset "{name}" to the default settings? Its key binding, lighting and pictures are lost.
prof_active_kbd: {name} is now the active keyboard profile
prof_active_mouse: {name} is now the active mouse profile
prof_active_pad: {name} is now the active DisplayPad profile
prof_migrated: {n} profiles taken over from the old version
prof_migrated_skipped: {n} old profiles not taken over: Settings, Import 3.x profile
prof_err_no_adapter: This device has no profile support yet
prof_err_limit: No more profiles fit on this device
prof_err_last_profile: The last profile cannot be deleted
prof_err_bad_file: This file is not a profile
prof_err_wrong_device: This profile is for another device
prof_err_no_data: There is nothing to export yet
prof_err_snapshot_failed: The device's settings could not be read
prof_err_busy: A profile change is already running
settings_profiles_hint: Profiles are on each device's page now (the "Profile" entry). Old 3.x profile folders can still be imported here.
upd_history_empty: This installation has no version history.
upd_history_english: The version notes are written in English.
settings_ui_classic_hint: The interface of BaseCamp Linux 3.x. You can come back in its settings.
settings_ui_classic_confirm: BaseCamp Linux starts again in the classic interface. Your settings stay as they are.
settings_ui_web_confirm: BaseCamp Linux starts again in the new interface. Your settings stay as they are.
remote_no_pads: No pads yet. Create a virtual pad in BaseCamp Linux on the PC, or plug in the DisplayPad.
remote_home_hint: Tip: put this page on your home screen (browser menu, "Add to Home screen").
remote_locked: The PC is locked. Unlock it to press keys from the phone.
remote_pad_gone: This pad was deleted on the PC.
remote_press_failed: The key could not be pressed: {err}
remote_offline: No connection to the PC. Is BaseCamp Linux running and remote access on?
remote_pair_intro: In BaseCamp Linux on the PC, open remote access in the settings, choose "Pair a device" and type the code shown there.
remote_pair_wrong: Wrong or expired code. Ask the PC for a new one.
remote_unpaired: This phone is no longer paired with the PC.
vp_delete_pad_msg: Delete "{name}" with all its pages and keys?
vp_empty: No virtual pad yet. Build one here and press its keys from your phone or with the mouse.
vp_hint_press: A click presses the key, as on the phone.
vp_hint_edit: A click picks the key to change.
vp_win_gone: This pad no longer exists. The window closes.
vp_win_failed: The pad could not be loaded: {err}
rset_intro: Phones in this network open the pads of this PC in their browser and press the keys.
rset_port_in_use: Port {port} is in use by another program.
rset_unencrypted: Use it in a network you trust: the connection is not encrypted.
rset_allow_shell_help: Covers shell, program and plugin actions. Even without it, keys and texts a phone sets can type on this PC: pair only your own devices.
rset_allow_locked: Phones may press keys while the PC is locked
rset_allow_locked_help: Keys then also run while the session is locked.
rset_lock_unwatched: The lock of this session cannot be followed here, so keys also run while the PC is locked.
rset_pair_off: Switch remote access on to pair a device.
rset_pair_how: Scan the QR code with the phone's camera, or open an address below on the phone and type the code.
rset_no_address: No network address found. Is the PC in a network?
rset_firewall_hint: If the phone cannot open the page, allow port {port} (TCP) in the PC's firewall.
rset_address_hint: If the phone loses the pairing after the PC got a new address, pair again with the code, or give the PC a fixed address in your router.
rset_remove_msg: Remove "{name}"? This phone can then no longer press keys until it is paired again.
